builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware
summary: STEALTH replaces bit-exact provably secure linguistic steganography, which requires sender and receiver to reproduce identical token probabilities, with an exponential-race token sampler plus a rateless spinal code decoded by beam search that tolerates probability mismatches across precision, quantization, hardware, tokenizers, and model families. The cost is added encoding/decoding complexity (keyed pseudorandom sampling, beam-search spinal decoding) and a lower effective payload than idealized bit-exact schemes, since redundancy absorbs token flips. Adoption can fail if the threat model shifts, if stronger steganalyzers emerge, or if the receiver's distribution diverges so far that race flips exceed the code's correction capacity, and cross-family robustness is empirical rather than guaranteed.
rationale: This is covert communication and steganalysis-evasion research rather than a production LLM efficiency or reliability technique, so it does not serve the reader's inference, cost, or quality goals and is not something to adopt in standard production practice.

claims.statement: STEALTH replaces bit-exact provably secure linguistic steganography, which requires sender and receiver to reproduce identical token probabilities, with an exponential-race token sampler plus a rateless spinal code decoded by beam search that tolerates probability mismatches across precision, quantization, hardware, tokenizers, and model families. The cost is added encoding/decoding complexity (keyed pseudorandom sampling, beam-search spinal decoding) and a lower effective payload than idealized bit-exact schemes, since redundancy absorbs token flips. Adoption can fail if the threat model shifts, if stronger steganalyzers emerge, or if the receiver's distribution diverges so far that race flips exceed the code's correction capacity, and cross-family robustness is empirical rather than guaranteed.
Carries far more payload per token than prior robust schemes; bit-exact baselines decode almost no messages under precision/hardware mismatch while STEALTH decodes every message tested.
